name: Milalai
overview: Milalai was a male Levite known for his role associated with musical instruments, as recorded in Nehemiah 12:36. His identification as a Levite places him within the tribe set apart for service in the temple, highlighting his involvement in worship through music. There are no additional notes providing further detail about his life or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Milalai appears only once in Scripture and does not have a recorded meaning or title associated with it. Therefore, the name is presented plainly without additional significance beyond its identification of this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Milalai as a descendant of Levi, affirming his tribal lineage. No other family relationships or connections are documented beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Milalai's significance lies in his contribution to the temple worship as a Levite musician. His presence in Nehemiah 12:36 underscores the importance of Levites in leading worship through music during the post-exilic restoration of Jerusalem. This role reflects the biblical emphasis on ordered and God-centered worship within the community of Israel.
